{
  "title": "Cookie consent options",
  "body": "<!-- Have you searched for similar issues on the repository?\r\nBefore submitting this issue, please visit our wiki for common ones: https://github.com/brave/browser-ios/wiki\r\nFor more, check out our community site: https://community.brave.com/ -->\r\n\r\n### Description: \r\nIn the EU, almost every website displays a pop up asking users to agree to their cookies. As a user this is v annoying. \r\nThere are many product that offer this consent management, one being Quantcast Choice (https://www.quantcast.com/gdpr/consent-management-solution/)\r\n\r\nCan we have an option in Privacy that allows users to not see these pop-ups?\r\nThe text can be something like: \r\nHide Cookie consent pop-ups\r\n\r\n\r\ncc @johnnyryan and @tomlowenthal for approval\r\n\r\n\r\n",
  "state": "closed",
  "closed_at": "2022-11-02T13:51:56Z",
  "updated_at": "2022-11-10T15:16:17Z"
}

    "id": 553129666,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-553129666",
    "body": "@kylehickinson there are two (2.5?) approaches here broadly:\r\n\r\n1) Do what Cliqz is doing and just auto tell the IAB the user doesn't consent by setting those cookies for users.  This has a bunch of nasty side effects, including it _undoes_ a lot of our 3p cookie protections (since need to notify these folks, via 3p cookie, that the user has opted out).  We'd need to punch a hole in shields (not impossible, but something to be very cautious about…).  It also wouldn't address non IAB folks, and other similar popups\r\n\r\n2) Do what @ryanbr does with [his anti-cookie message list](https://www.fanboy.co.nz/fanboy-cookiemonster.txt), which is basically block as much related to the whole system as possible, at any possible vantage point (cosmetic, network, etc).  This has the benefit of being pretty easy to deply given our current infrastructure, but I think would cut against  @johnnyryan's legal concerns (it also has the typical coverage concerns of filter lists, but thats a \"solveable problem\" [hand wave])\r\n\r\nThere are a couple of hybrid options we could consider\r\n- Still keep the 3p cookie blocking with shields (e.g. don't punch an IAB sized hole in them) but just have the browser inject the relevant cookie into those network requests.\r\n\r\n- go hard on the filter lists, i can build up automation to target these kinds of annoyances.  Would be an interesting Brave distinguishing feature (again assuming it doesn't make us go to jail, re @johnnyryan jkjkjkjkj)\r\n\r\nIf none of those appeal, let me know and I can keep brainstorming",
    "created_at": "2019-11-12T21:44:12Z",
    "updated_at": "2019-11-12T21:44:12Z"
  },

    "body": "There is no short term iOS plan currently.  In brave-core, the immediate option is for users to enable the cookie blocking filter list in brave://adblock (knowing it comes with some webcompat risk).  The longer term option is to build smaller, higher confidence list we can check through automation.\r\n\r\nFor iOS the possible paths i can see are either:\r\n1. enable custom filter lists on iOS (so that iOS users can enable the same useful-but-sometimes-webcompat-risking), and / or\r\n2. wait until we have a higher confidence list (no immediate time frame) and we can incorporate that into the default iOS filter lists",

    "html_url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-1309472376",
    "body": "Verified using version `1.45 (22.11.8.15)` on the following device(s):\r\n\r\niPhone 12 - iOS 16.x\r\niPhone XR - iOS 15.x \r\niPhone X - iOS 14.x\r\niPads - iPadOS 16.x, 15.x\r\n\r\nAcceptance Criteria: https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/pull/5839#issue-1336364313\r\n\r\nCase: user clicks on \"Yes block cookie consent notices\" on the popup:\r\n\r\n - Verified that the setting is enabled in shields\r\n - Verified the cookie notice blocking filter list is enabled\r\n - Verified the animation plays and then the popup disappears\r\n \r\nCase: user clicks on \"No thanks\" on the popup\r\n\r\n- Verified the setting is not enabled in shields\r\n- Verified the cookie notice blocking filter list is not enabled\r\n- Verified the popup is dismissed\r\n\r\nCase: User enables the settings:\r\n\r\n- Verified - the popup doesn't appear on second launch (Note: you will need to enabled it on first launch)\r\n- Verified -  the cookie consent notices are blocked\r\n\r\nCase: When the setting is not enabled:\r\n\r\n - Verified - the popup appears on a second launch (note that depending on timing other full screen popups might appear in priority)\r\n - Verified - Cookie consent notices are not blocked\r\n\r\n- Verified synchronization between the cookie blocking setting in shields and the filter list is enabled in filter lists screen\r\n- Verified setting is held when app is terminated/relaunched.\r\n\r\nExample | Example | Example | Example | Example\r\n-|-|-|-|-\r\n![IMG_4091](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17885425/200957599-0b7bdb7d-e726-449e-b9a9-7ac36e21b1ed.PNG) | ![IMG_4092](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17885425/200957603-5947212d-26d9-42cc-beba-cc5d496bb036.PNG) | ![IMG_4093](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17885425/200957606-886f65cb-2dd1-4c5b-829a-094a8dc9dbbb.PNG) | ![IMG_4082](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17885425/200957685-fe27c31b-64f0-44a5-b1f0-2da30f4dfa91.PNG) | ![IMG_4095](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17885425/200958053-60f94ea5-c718-4dc7-a744-29a57bb09448.PNG)\r\n\r\nExample | Example | Example | Example\r\n-|-|-|-\r\n![IMG_0027 2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17885425/200958853-2f5bec35-fd30-4aa3-adfb-6f17f23d3dee.PNG) | ![IMG_0028](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17885425/200958856-7ea996ef-bd98-4f4d-8d65-1393b4be867a.PNG) | ![IMG_0029 2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17885425/200959009-71024d08-f583-47d3-ba52-89e2a99f6625.PNG) | ![IMG_0030 2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17885425/200959028-6535381c-baf5-4ce2-a80c-3f0dd1c75ada.PNG)\r\n",
